title: Lester learns the names of chords in Basie's band
summary: Lester played changes by ear and only in Basie's band learned their names from Buck Clayton and Count Basie; Phillips says it changed nothing in his playing.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: What do you mean by "lately?"
Well, after he got with Basie and the bands, and started playing changes, name them -- E-Flat-Seventh and G-Minor-Seventh and all that.
He started getting into changes?
He tried learning what they was. He knew what they was. He was playing them...
He tried to learn what they were so he could get them..
He wanted to know the names of them.
When did he start to do this? Did he ever tell you about this?
Yeah, when he was with Basie.
Did anybody give him lessons? Or was he just doing this
Phillips - 155
on his own?

No, he said at that time... At that time, too. Because when I first started playing, you didn't hear no cats talkin' about no changes. What kind of changes? You played them, but you didn't hear nobody calling them. You didn't even see no chord changes on no music. You know what I mean? At that time, they started naming... He wanted to know what the name of it was. He learned the names of all the changes.
He did learn them all.
Yeah, he knew them now. I mean, then...
Was he into Ninth chords and Elevenths and Thirteenths?
Yeah. Oh, everything about the chords. Because he had guys in there that knew it. Buck Clayton... Buck Clayton was an arranger.
Yeah, I was wondering. Did these guys help him any to learn the chords? How did he go about it?
He sat down with Buck. They would play them and tell him what he was playing -- put a name on it.
Just play it on a trumpet or on the piano?

He'd play them on his horn. He'd play it, but he didn't know the name. He just know what notes he started on and everything, but he didn't know... He just had that ear. Like, he'd play a tune that he didn't even know the name of, but he still could play the changes in it. Or he
Phillips - 156
would put some extra changes in it. But he said then he learned them.
And Count, too. I think he said Count would sit down at the piano, too, and learn him. Taught him the name of the chords.
When was this? What year?
I don't know what year it was.
He told you this later on? Is that what you're saying?

Yeah. He told me later on about how he learned the name of chord changes. He said, 'I've been playing this stuff all the time. I just learned the names. But I've been playing it all the time!' I said, 'Yeah.'
How much later on after he learned it did he tell you that he'd learned it?
He told me when he was learning it.
Oh, he told you when he was in Basie's band.
Yeah, when he was in Basie's band.
How long did that go on?
I don't know. He never said no more about it. It just come up, you know. Something had come up and he was talking about changes.
Did he do anything differently as a result of that?
No. He didn't have to do nothin' different, because he was already playin' it! All he wanted to know was the name. He said he wanted to know when he was
Phillips - 157
making B-Flat-Seventh or E-Flat-Seventh or Augmented Ninth -- he said he wanted to know what it was. He was making it all the time, but he wanted to know the names of it.
